incidents.title: Concurrent commits overwrote session._changes; IN + CASE caused nondeterministic search order
incidents.description: Two interconnected production issues: (1) Flask-SQLAlchemy sessions were shared across concurrent requests, causing session._changes overwrites that lost index updates. (2) Database-specific IN clause optimization reordered search results unpredictably.
root_causes: Shared mutable state (session._changes) without per-transaction isolation
Hardcoded SQL CASE WHEN ordering, which differs across MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQLite
Rigid event listener registration requiring manual model setup

code: # Thread A: commit post with body='Update from thread A'
# Thread B (reused session): commit post with body='Update from thread B'
# Thread B overwrites session._changes before Thread A's index update completes
db.session.commit()  # session._changes = [q], Thread A's [p] is LOST
# Result: Only 'Update from thread B' indexed; 'Update from thread A' missing from search
log_output: Index content mismatch after concurrent commits.
Search result order inconsistent with backend IDs.
Post A created by user but does not appear in search results.

code: # Backend (Elasticsearch) returns IDs in relevance order: [5, 2, 3]
# Construct SQL to preserve order using CASE WHEN
# MySQL optimizes IN clause and reorders to [2, 3, 5]
# Result: same query, different order on different databases
log_output: Search result order [2, 3, 5] differs from backend [5, 2, 3].
User pagination broken: page 2 contains items from page 1.
Ranking signals ignored due to database reordering.

incidents.expected_result: Transactions update the index independently without overwrites; search results follow backend order exactly across all SQL databases; new mixin subclasses are automatically indexed.

fix_strategies_applied.justification: session.info is transaction-local and per-instance; each request has its own session instance in production.

fix_strategies_applied.strategy: Reorder results in Python using dict lookup instead of SQL CASE WHEN
fix_strategies_applied.justification: Python's dict insertion order (3.7+) is guaranteed; O(n) lookup is faster than SQL CASE, avoids database-specific optimization quirks.
fix_strategies_applied.impact: Deterministic ordering across MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQLite; deduplicates and handles missing IDs gracefully.

fix_strategies_applied.strategy: Use __init_subclass__() to auto-register mixin subclasses; listen on db.Session class, not instance
fix_strategies_applied.justification: Metaclass hook captures all subclasses; isinstance check works for all present and future subclasses.
fix_strategies_applied.impact: New models automatically indexed without manual setup; zero registration burden.

known_issues_and_limitations.impact: After deployment, reindex from database to ensure consistency
known_issues_and_limitations.mitigation: Rebuild is one-time cost; subsequent indexing is automatic and concurrent-safe

known_issues_and_limitations.issue: Python dict reordering adds O(n) overhead
known_issues_and_limitations.impact: For each search, n dict lookups + list reordering
known_issues_and_limitations.mitigation: For n < 1000 (typical pagination), overhead < 1ms. Faster than SQL CASE WHEN overhead.

known_issues_and_limitations.impact: Tested on SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL. Other databases untested.
known_issues_and_limitations.mitigation: Solution uses only standard SQL features; should work on any DBMS with IN clause

known_issues_and_limitations.mitigation: Tests validate logic; integration tests with real backends recommended before production
known_issues_and_limitations.note: Tests confirm behavior of refactored mixin; real backend behavior needs separate validation
